lesson.title: The vous Register
lesson.subtitle: When vous is required; vous voulez vs tu veux and the universal -ez ending.

hook.title: Switching Gears Between tu and vous in the Same Room
hook.content: Flip between informal tu (-es/-s/-x) for a friend and polite/plural vous (-ez / êtes) for a stranger or any group of two or more people!

footnotes.title: Why vous is also the plural of tu
footnotes.content: Addressing two or more friends at once always uses plural vous (tu + tu = vous)!

pattern.title: The Instant Switch: tu (-s/-x) ↔ vous (-ez)
pattern.content: Flip sentences between tu parles ↔ vous parlez, tu veux ↔ vous voulez, tu as ↔ vous avez, tu vas ↔ vous allez, tu es ↔ vous êtes.
pattern.linguist_note: Second-person plural -ez (/e/) is the most regular inflectional suffix in the French verbal system.
pattern.trap_note: Don't mix tu with -ez (*tu parlez) or vous with -s (*vous parles)!

exercises.prompt: Match each informal tu question with its polite/plural vous twin:
exercises.target_answer: Vous parlez français ?, Vous voulez partir ?, Vous avez le billet ?, Vous allez à Paris ?, Vous êtes ici ?
exercises.meaning: Tu parles français ?, Tu veux partir ?, Tu as le billet ?, Tu vas à Paris ?, Tu es ici ?
exercises.explanation: Four out of five simply end in -ez (/e/) with vous; only être uses êtes.

exercises.prompt: You are talking to two close friends at once. Which pronoun and verb do you use for 'Are you two going to the cinema?'
exercises.meaning: Are you (plural) going to the cinema?
exercises.explanation: Addressing two or more people always uses plural vous!

exercises.prompt: Convert from informal 'Tu parles anglais' to polite/plural vous:
exercises.explanation: parles (/paʁl/) adds the /e/ sound in vous parlez (/vu paʁle/).

exercises.idea: do you speak French or English (polite vous)
cues: You speak French → Vous parlez français
exercises.meaning: Do you speak French or English?
exercises.explanation: ou ('or') has no accent, whereas où ('where') has a grave accent!

diagnosis.slip: used où with an accent for 'or'

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: Vous voulez aller au restaurant avec nous
exercises.target_answer: Vous voulez aller au restaurant avec nous
exercises.meaning: Do you want to go to the restaurant with us?
exercises.explanation: voulez (-ez) pulls the bare infinitive aller (-er).
exercises.affirmation: You paired Vous voulez with aller and avec nous.

summary.outcome: Switch effortlessly between informal tu and polite/plural vous across regular and core verbs.

use_example.german: Tu viens ? — Oui ! Et vous, vous venez avec nous ?
use_example.english: Are you coming? — Yes! And you all, are you coming with us?

summary.takeaway: One friend is tu; one stranger is vous; two of anybody is vous.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on Le Pont ([10] avoir & the H It Lost): see how The vous Register leads directly into avoir & the H It Lost.

twist.prompt: Think it through again without looking back — express "Do you speak French or English" in French:
twist.explanation: Re-constructing "Vous parlez français ou anglais" from the underlying rule cements the pattern of The vous Register.

vous.etymology_derivation: Latin vōs 'you all' promoted to politeness — the same T–V ladder as German Sie and English's lost 'ye'.

tu.etymology_derivation: Latin tū — the very word the King James Bible still whispers as thou. Point your lips; the vowel is not English's.

voulez.etymology_derivation: Every French verb (except être, dire, faire) ends in -ez with vous!

êtes.etymology_derivation: Old French estes → êtes: the circumflex hat marks the vanished s.

avez.etymology_derivation: In liaison, the s of vous buzzes as /z/: vous‿avez /vu.za.ve/.

allez.etymology_derivation: Also shouted at sports matches: 'Allez !' ('Come on!').

français.etymology_derivation: Not capitalized when naming the language in French.
